correctness.rationale: For every odd prime p and r>=1, the path polynomial collapses to (z²−4)^((p^r−1)/2), and endpoint cyclicity gives one Jordan block per sign. The grid Kronecker sum reduces to four identical nilpotent tensor-sum blocks at eigenvalues 4, 0, 0, −4. A written integer Toeplitz-determinant formula and prime-power Legendre cancellation prove strong Lefschetz and odd-length block partitions even when p is small relative to grid side. Fitting decomposition gives the exact entrance distribution; the eigenvalue-order and p-adic exponent kernel argument proves every fixed-point count and Möbius inversion gives the joint census and sharp maximal period. The three delivered standalone programs verify independent finite matrix/rank/determinant instances; the universal conclusion rests on the algebraic proof. Scientific limit: characteristic two and other grid dimensions are excluded.

value.rationale: Open square lattices are canonical finite local cellular automata. In odd characteristic, knowing singularity or nullity alone does not determine the transient lengths, primitive periods or counts of trajectories entering each period. The theorem resolves all of these for the natural infinite prime-power side-length family, with an explicit full Jordan form, exact joint census, attained maximal period and extremal transient population; the special family is driven by a nontrivial Frobenius/Chebyshev collapse. This is a motivated complete classification, not a chosen arbitrary finite example or a known-table recomputation.
